note: Practical buyer comparison aids, not equipment/certification or stock claims

applications/everyday-hydration.title: Everyday bottle selection: four real-world checks
applications/everyday-hydration.intro: A commuter bottle is selected for repeated filling, cleaning, bag storage and carrying, not simply the largest printed volume.
rows: Bag or desk fit
A tall bottle can be awkward even when its milliliter volume looks modest
Check actual height, base diameter and cup-holder or bag clearance
Lid access
One-handed opening may be convenient but affects cap complexity
Test the cap with a filled sample and the intended users
Cleaning
Small joints and removable straws influence cleaning access
Request instructions for each part and inspect reassembly
Repeated purchasing
A brand needs consistent cap and color revisions
Save the exact factory model and accepted parts list

applications/gym-sports.title: Gym-use bottles versus protein shakers
applications/gym-sports.intro: A water bottle and a mixing shaker solve different purchase needs even when both are sold to fitness channels.
rows: Plain hydration
Simple drinking and low accessory count
Choose source sports models and validate lid design
Powder mixing
Mixing component and removable closure are key
Check what is supplied with shaker models and shake-test a sample
Locker-bag transport
Cap leakage and carrying design affect buyer complaints
Test the real filled bottle in sideways positions
Gym merchandising
Brand decoration must survive handling and cleaning
Approve artwork and actual printed sample before bulk order

applications/kids-school.title: School bottle sourcing: needs vary by age and market
applications/kids-school.intro: Child-facing product approval should start with intended age, removable parts, the drinking method and cleaning access.
rows: Younger users
Complex lids can be hard to operate or clean
Review age-market safety needs and sample with adult supervision
School-bag use
Straw and valve closure leakage can affect books and bags
Test a completed sample rather than trusting photos
Shared or repeated use
Labels, removable parts and cleaning instructions matter
Agree product warnings and part documentation
School branding
Small artwork can lose clarity on shaped surfaces
Review final art and a decorated sample

applications/outdoor-travel.title: Outdoor and travel: assess the filled product
applications/outdoor-travel.intro: Actual filled weight, carrying attachment and exposure to movement can determine whether a bottle is suitable.
rows: Trail carrying
Filled balance can be more important than label volume
Inspect full sample and handle/strap attachment
Car or transport use
Fit, side orientation and closure security vary
Measure external dimensions and test cap configuration
Temperature exposure
Material grade and seals have different permitted use ranges
Request confirmed resin and temperature instructions
Travel packing
Multiple items and larger volumes change freight and carton requirements
Confirm actual carton packing and pallet data

applications/promotional-gifts.title: Promotional campaigns: approve three separate deliverables
applications/promotional-gifts.intro: Campaign deadlines are best managed by freezing the decorated bottle, individual gift packaging and carton label as separate revisions.
rows: Product choice
The pictured color or capacity may not match the order variant
Match factory code and sample to the quotation
Printed logo
Screen, digital and transfer effects vary by substrate
Check print method, position, adhesion and color
Gift packing
Unboxing quality and carton volume affect landed cost
Approve real box dieline and inner protection
Delivery coordination
A fixed campaign date requires an agreed production plan
Record signed sample, quantities and shipping terms

features/straw-lid.title: Straw lid: compare hygiene and assembly details
features/straw-lid.intro: A straw lid should be assessed as a removable assembly rather than a single marketing feature.
rows: Straw geometry
Bent, long or soft parts can change flow and cleaning
Check length and replacement availability on the exact model
Mouthpiece
Open/close operation influences usability
Test sealing and accessible cleaning areas
Seal and joints
More interfaces create more components to maintain
Request component breakdown and reassembly instructions
Age-market fit
Removable parts may require market-specific review
Confirm destination requirements before school procurement

features/flip-top.title: Flip-top: design variables buyers should test
features/flip-top.intro: A hinge, latch, spring or seal can affect the experience more than the visual flip-top style.
rows: Opening method
Latch force and travel differ by model
Test actual cap using intended users
Seal position
Leak paths can occur around the mouthpiece or threads
Record the filled sample and agreed leak test
Hinge fatigue
Repeated opening may affect function
Agree opening-cycle acceptance method if necessary
Cleaning
Hidden hinge areas and seals may retain residue
Review part accessibility and cleaning instructions

features/carry-handle.title: Carry attachment: choose the actual full-bottle load
features/carry-handle.intro: Handle, loop and strap products cannot be evaluated from empty catalog photography alone.
rows: Handle grip
Grip shape changes carrying comfort when full
Compare an actual filled sample
Loop or strap
Attachment, removability and secure fit matter
Request exact included component list
Load behavior
Weight increases with capacity and contents
Do not claim load rating without tested supplier evidence
Carton packaging
Protruding handles affect carton fit
Inspect final outer carton layout

features/large-capacity.title: Large-capacity selection: volume is only the starting point
features/large-capacity.intro: Two large jugs with similar printed capacity can differ greatly in carrying balance, closure access and landed freight.
rows: Usable volume
Nominal capacity and comfortable fill may differ
Validate fill instructions and source milliliters
Handle leverage
A full jug requires safe grip and stable base
Compare real filled samples
Mouthpiece design
Large body size does not imply easy one-handed drinking
Test spout, straw or cap version
Export carton
Cube and carton quantity influence freight cost
Obtain measured packed dimensions

features/gradient-colors.title: Gradient-color approval: a photo is not a color master
features/gradient-colors.intro: Gradient plastic finish should be reviewed under consistent light and against a physical master reference, especially with custom logos.
rows: Resin color
Pigment and translucency change visual appearance
Approve the actual molded sample
Color transition
Gradient start and end position affect design consistency
Agree color master and tolerance with manufacturer
Logo contrast
Text can become unreadable against variable backgrounds
Check physical print on both light and dark zones
Repeat orders
Finish control needs a retained signed reference
Keep production revision and accepted sample
